acceptanceCriteria: A row that expanded to its enclosing declaration names both the hit line range and the returned span range.
Expansion never crosses a file boundary and never exceeds the line budget; when it would, the row falls back to the hit range with an explicit reason.
Measured on the frozen retrieval evaluation at fixed byte budgets with no recall regression.
body: Owner requested this on 2026-09-23 after reviewing Tencent/WeKnora (MIT) as prior art; this ticket records an idea, not delivery or promotion. Original Go work only; no source import. WeKnora is an LLM-at-ingest, database-backed RAG platform, so only the mechanism is borrowed and it must stay deterministic, local and read-only under AGENTS.md invariants 4 and 7. Before implementation is called complete, update the owning indexed spec with stable requirements, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence and rollback, and finish normal CEM/OCM, independent review and mandatory gates. Prior art: website-docs/03-features/04-chunking.md of https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora. With parent-child chunking only child chunks (384 chars, 20% overlap) enter the vector and BM25 indexes; a hit returns the parent block (4096 chars) that carries `parent_chunk_id`, giving small-window precision with large-window context. Current state: rows are path plus line range and a lexical hit returns the matched lines only, so the agent re-reads the file to see the enclosing function. V1-0098 asks for span ranking under a line budget and a sufficiency check; this ticket narrows to the retrieval rule. Idea: match at line or declaration granularity, resolve each hit to its enclosing declaration from the existing language-symbol parse, return the declaration span under the line budget, and keep the hit line visible in the row so the inclusion reason stays exact. Owning spec: docs/specs/task-context-packet-v0.md. Related: V1-0098.
title: context: match on small units, return the enclosing declaration (parent-child retrieval)
